ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle JKL, K is above, JL is the base, and M is located on base JL. Sides JK and KL are both labeled 11; a perpendicular line is drawn from K to M, with a right angle mark at M; the segment ML on the right side of the base is labeled 5.5; the angle at J is labeled 60°. Reasoning: Because JK = KL, triangle JKL is an isosceles triangle. KM is the altitude drawn from vertex K to base JL, and in an isosceles triangle, the altitude from the vertex to the base also bisects the base, so M is the midpoint of JL. Therefore JM = ML. In the figure ML = 5.5, so JM = 5.5.
